candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — systems-based analysis of safety events
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate system-focused event investigation from individual-blame review and prospective FMEA by recognizing its emphasis on contributing system factors and process redesign after an adverse event or near miss.

options.A: Individual-fault review focused primarily on identifying and retraining the person who made the final error.
options.B: Failure modes and effects analysis used prospectively to predict how a process could fail before an event occurs.
options.C: A no-accountability model in which individual training, preparation, and behavior are never considered during event review.
options.D: System-focused event investigation and analysis aimed at identifying contributing system factors and developing safer, sustainable solutions.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ's CANDOR System-Focused Event Investigation and Analysis Guide describes a systems approach that examines contributing factors such as staffing, technology, equipment, environment, communication, teamwork, and task/process design so that safer and more sustainable solutions can be developed. D therefore matches the scenario. A is too narrow and reflects the individual-blame/retraining approach AHRQ warns may fail to produce sustained improvement. B describes a prospective risk-analysis method rather than retrospective investigation of an event that already occurred. C is also incorrect because AHRQ explicitly states that a systems approach is not a blame-free culture and does not eliminate individual accountability for training, preparation, and behavior.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AHRQ's system-focused event investigation seeks contributing system factors rather than reflexive individual blame and examines organization/staffing, technology, equipment, environment, communication, teamwork, and task/process design to develop sustainable safety solutions; the approach retains appropriate individual accountability.
